ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Calculate current I\(_2\) in this Darlington pair circuit, assuming a typical forward base-emitter junction voltage drop of 0.7 volts for each transistor. The current I\(_2\) is ______ mA.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit diagram, the left side is a 19 V power supply, with the lower end grounded; the upper/left node is connected to the base of the first NPN transistor, and the two transistors form a Darlington connection. The first transistor is labeled β = 85, and its emitter drives the base of the second transistor. The second transistor is labeled β = 30, and its emitter is grounded through a 150 Ω resistor. The red arrow I2 is located in the collector branch of the second transistor, representing the collector current of the second transistor. Reasoning: The forward base-emitter voltage drop of each transistor is taken as 0.7 V. In the Darlington structure, the emitter voltage of the second transistor is 19 V - 0.7 V - 0.7 V = 17.6 V. This voltage is applied across the 150 Ω resistor, so the emitter current of the second transistor is I_E2 = 17.6 / 150 = 0.11733 A. Because I2 is the collector current of the second transistor, and β = 30, I_C2 = β/(β+1) × I_E2 = 30/31 × 0.11733 A = 0.1135 A = 113.5 mA.
